items.title: How to survive in an AI world?
items.subtitle: A friendly guide to using AI while keeping your own ideas and choices.
items.imageAlt: A person and a friendly glowing assistant sharing ideas at a table
items.intro: AI can feel like a big change, but you do not need to be a computer expert to use it. Think of it as a helpful assistant: it can explain, suggest and organise, while you stay in charge.

points.title: Learn to live with AI
points.text: Let AI help with small, everyday jobs. You can ask it to explain a confusing letter, plan a simple meal, or make a packing list.
points.example: Try: “Help me make a shopping list for three easy dinners.”

points.title: Learn to think with AI
points.text: Use it to explore ideas, ask questions and see different options. Tell it what matters to you, then decide which suggestions fit.
points.example: Try: “Give me three low-cost ideas for a day out with my family.”

points.title: Learn to keep your own judgement
points.text: AI can sound sure even when it is mistaken. Treat its answer as a starting point and check important details before acting.
points.example: For a health, money or safety decision, check a trusted expert or official source too.

points.title: Start with one useful task
points.text: You do not have to learn everything at once. Pick one task that takes you time and see whether AI can make it easier.
points.example: Ask it to turn a long message into three short points.

points.title: Keep private details private
points.text: Do not paste passwords, bank details or private information into a tool unless you understand how it will be used.
points.example: You can remove names and account numbers before asking for help with a document.

items.takeaway: Use AI to make everyday life a little easier. Stay curious, check what matters, and keep the final choice yours.

items.title: Make AI your thinking partner
items.subtitle: Get help with a blank page without handing over the steering wheel.
items.imageAlt: A person sorting colourful idea cards with help from a friendly assistant
items.intro: AI is most useful when you bring the goal and it helps you explore the next step. You do not need special words: describe what you are trying to do as if you were asking a helpful person.

points.title: Say what you are trying to do
points.text: A little context helps the answer fit your real situation. Mention who it is for, what you need, and any limits such as time or cost.
points.example: “I have 20 minutes and basic ingredients. Suggest a simple lunch for two.”

points.title: Ask for a few choices
points.text: Instead of accepting the first suggestion, ask for alternatives. Comparing choices makes it easier to notice what works for you.
points.example: “Give me a simpler version and one that costs less.”

points.title: Improve the answer together
points.text: You can say what is missing and ask for another try. A conversation can be more useful than one perfect question.
points.example: “That is helpful. Please make it warmer and keep it under 100 words.”

points.title: Add your own experience
points.text: AI does not know your people, your neighbourhood or your personal history unless you explain it. Your experience is part of the answer.
points.example: Read a draft aloud and change anything that does not sound like you.

items.takeaway: You set the destination. AI can help you find a few routes, and you choose the one that feels right.

items.title: How to check an AI answer
items.subtitle: A simple pause can help you spot an answer that needs a second look.
items.imageAlt: A person using a magnifying glass to check a simple list of facts
items.intro: AI tools can make mistakes, leave out important details, or use old information. A few quick checks can help you decide whether an answer is ready to use.

points.title: Notice when the answer really matters
points.text: A dinner idea is low risk. Advice about medicine, money, legal matters or personal safety deserves more care.
points.example: Use AI to prepare questions for a professional, not to replace their advice.

points.title: Look for a reliable source
points.text: Ask where the information came from, then open the source yourself. A link is useful only if it really supports the claim.
points.example: For a government service, check the official government website.

points.title: Check the date and details
points.text: Rules, prices and news can change. Make sure the page is recent and that names, numbers and dates match.
points.example: If an answer mentions a deadline, confirm it on the organisation’s own page.

points.title: Ask another trusted person
points.text: If you are still unsure, ask someone knowledgeable. It is sensible to pause before sharing or acting on something important.
points.example: For urgent health concerns, contact a qualified health professional.

items.takeaway: Let AI help you get started, then verify important information before you rely on it.
